card: A passive participle describes what was done *to* something: **прочи́танная кни́га** = *a book that has been read*. The past passive is the common one: **-нный** or **-тый** (**прочита́ть → прочи́танный**, **откры́ть → откры́тый**). Its short form makes the everyday passive: **Магази́н закры́т.** **Письмо́ напи́сано.**

sections.body: The short past passive participle is everyday Russian: on signs (**Закры́то**), in the news (**Мост постро́ен**) and when a job is done (**Всё сде́лано!**). The long forms belong to writing.

sections.title: Short forms make the passive
sections.body: Short forms agree with the subject: **Дверь откры́та.** **О́кна закры́ты.** Tense comes from **быть**: **Дом был постро́ен в 1900 году́.** **Рабо́та бу́дет зако́нчена за́втра.** The doer goes in the instrumental: **стихи́, напи́санные Пу́шкиным**.

sections.title: Present passive
sections.body: **-емый** or **-имый**, from imperfective verbs: **чита́емый** (*widely read*), **люби́мый** (*loved, favourite*). Many have become plain adjectives: **люби́мый**, **уважа́емый** (*dear*, opening a letter), **необходи́мый**.

sections.title: One н or two?
sections.body: Long participles have **-нн-**: **прочи́танная кни́га**. Short forms have one **н**: **кни́га прочи́тана**. Adjectives from imperfective verbs without a prefix have one **н**: **жа́реная карто́шка**; the prefixed participle has two: **поджа́ренная**.

mistakes.why: A current state uses the short form: **закры́т**.
The short form agrees with **письмо́**, which is neuter.
The doer of a passive is in the instrumental.

examples.ru: Э́тот мост был постро́ен сто лет наза́д.
examples.en: This bridge was built a hundred years ago.
Everyone knows the poems written by Pushkin.
